uster: An’ now that she’s here an’ workin’ an’ that nigger’s well again, what does he do but go out an’ get drunk worse than he uster with his wife.
usta: "Like I is any mamby-pamby ooman, like I ain't usta to takin' care o' meself."
"We usta catch dem in Low'rd, too--but I don't like dem.
ust:
Whah de little birds in spring,
Ust to come an' drink an' sing,
An' de chillen waded on dey way to school.

But I t'ink I 'd lak it better to be down in Jones's wood,
Where we ust to have sich frolics, Lucy, you an' me an' Nelse,
Dough my appetite 'ud call me, ef dey was n't nuffin else.

An' let me feel dat ol' delight
I ust to in dey glee.
But hyeah we is, my pipe an' me,
